reason: The cited evidence does not address CoCrFeNi composites with ceramic/graphite reinforcements, nor does it demonstrate the claimed synergy or specific tribofilm mechanisms. E1 shows wear resistance in a different alloy via a nanohierarchical structure, E2 and E3 concern a TMD-HEA lubricant coating, E4 mentions HEA composites but not tribology, and E5 discusses grain-size-dependent friction in bare CoCrFeMnNi. None of the key premises are supported by the cited passages.
premises: Ceramic particles provide dispersion strengthening and wear resistance in a CoCrFeNi matrix
Graphite particles form a lubricious carbon-based tribofilm during sliding
The graphite tribofilm becomes active and reduces friction at elevated temperatures
Synergy between ceramic and graphite particles maintains stable tribological performance from RT to 800 °C
The composite will reduce friction by 20–30% and wear rate by an order of magnitude versus unreinforced CoCrFeNi
